acceptance: When a throughput phase object exists, the exported Throughput@Size equals phase.throughput_at_size and is absent when phase.success is false
Power@Size uses only power-test rows (filter by test type), with a test for a combined run with iterations=1
QphH/QphDS is absent whenever either input is withheld
Regression tests cover a phase with success=False and no FAILED rows
context: 2026-10-04 throughput adversarial review (develop 8ed0c64e1). Builder code read directly; both defects reproduced by reviewer probes.
description:
`benchbox/core/results/builder.py:800-814` recomputes Throughput@Size from `phase.total_queries_executed` and `phase.duration_ms` but never reads `phase.success` or `phase.throughput_at_size`. The adapter correctly withholds the metric when a stream fails (adapter.py:1126-1131, result_capture.py:1742, throughput/runner.py:488-494), but `result_factory.build_enhanced_benchmark_result` rebuilds metrics from scratch.

Effect: if a stream times out or is cancelled before starting, it leaves no FAILED rows, so the failed-query gate does not fire and a score from partial work is exported. A reviewer's probe produced 7920 for a phase with success=False.

Related, same file: `_calculate_power_at_size` (builder.py:826-842) takes the latest iteration of all `run_type == "measurement"` rows. Throughput rows have no iteration and default to 1, so a combined power+throughput run with iterations=1 mixes S x 22 concurrent query times into the power geometric mean (probe: 7756 instead of 36000), and QphH is wrong. The default of 3 iterations hides it.
